ai.title: Don't Blame The Preferences: Examining The Emergence of Sycophancy in LLM Training
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.10045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI sycophancy, the tendency of large language models (LLMs) to flatter users and affirm their beliefs, can undermine accuracy and contribute to misinformation, dependence, and overconfidence. Although prior work has benchmarked sycophancy in released models and proposed mitigations, its origins during training remain poorly understood. Preference alignment methods such as RLHF and DPO are often blamed, but their effects are rarely compared with earlier training stages. We investigate sycophancy across the training pipelines of three model families and three benchmarks. We find that sycophancy is largely established by the end of supervised fine-tuning (SFT), rather than introduced by preference alignment. Across all nine model benchmark combinations, SFT checkpoints attain at least 92% of preference aligned models' sycophancy scores and at least 85% of final models' scores; on average, they are about as sycophantic as final models. Preference alignment increases sycophancy in only four of nine cases, by an average of 4.2 percentage points when it does. To probe the underlying causes, we isolate model representations associated with sycophancy using mechanistic interpretability and measure their activation on training datasets from each stage. ai.title: Restoring General and Improving Domain-Specific Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs Without Retraining
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.10279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety-aligned language models are known to suffer degradation in refusal behavior following domain-specific fine-tuning, even when the fine-tuning data is entirely benign. The predominant mitigation strategy, preference optimization on the fine-tuned model, is computationally expensive and requires domain-specific preference data that is often unavailable in practice. We propose SPECTRA, a training-free, weight-level method that restores refusal behavior by transferring the base model's refusal direction into the fine-tuned model's weights via an activation-aware, low-rank update, requiring no gradient-based optimization or domain-specific safety data. The low-rank design restricts the intervention to the subspace most causally active on harmful inputs, leaving benign behavior largely undisturbed by construction. Empirically, SPECTRA substantially improves refusal behavior across a comprehensive safety evaluation, while preserving general coherence, domain-specific knowledge, and producing negligible change in false refusal rates.

ai.title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.10329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly drive systems research and rely on simulators to evaluate candidate designs at scale. Simulators are imperfect by design: their modeling limitations can distort predictions yet leave the recommended design correct, or change which design should be selected. We introduce Siris to test whether LLMs can tell these cases apart, judging from their systems understanding when a limitation invalidates the simulator's recommendation. By perturbing a simulator, Siris constructs workload pairs with the same candidates, limitation, and simulator recommendation. The perturbation changes predictions on both workloads, yet a reference simulator supports the recommendation on only one. Evaluating thirteen frontier LLMs on LLM serving design problems, we find that identifying a limitation does not ensure a correct choice, and even the strongest models sometimes abandon valid recommendations. Self-correction through a review turn helps these models restore valid choices but introduces new errors in several others. These findings motivate evaluating systems understanding through design decisions under imperfect simulators.
ai.summary: LLM agents increasingly drive systems research and rely on simulators to evaluate candidate designs at scale.

ai.title: Beyond the Prompt: Leveraging Pre-Decoding States for Jailbreak Detection in dLLMs
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.10258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have recently emerged as a strong alternative to autoregressive models, generating responses by iteratively refining masked tokens in parallel rather than decoding sequentially. While enabling more efficient and flexible inference, dLLMs remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, including recent attacks that exploit properties unique to dLLMs such as bidirectional conditioning and parallel masked-token refinement. In this work, we show that these same properties also expose a safety-relevant detection surface absent from standard autoregressive decoding: even when a jailbreak is difficult to identify from prompt representations alone, it can still be detected from hidden states over masked response positions before any tokens are generated. By training linear classifiers on prompt and pre-decoding response representations, we empirically show that neither view strictly dominates, with each detecting attacks that the other misses. We introduce $\texttt{ReFuse}$ (Representation Fusion), an inference-time detector that fuses the sigmoid harmfulness scores of the two classifiers. Without modifying model weights or the decoding procedure, $\texttt{ReFuse}$ reduces average ASR across multiple jailbreaks from 63.29% for the undefended model and 11.27% for a prompt-only classifier to 3.31%, while keeping average benign refusal on standard utility benchmarks below 1% on LLaDA-8B. ai.title: Policy Over Purpose: Auditing LLM Content Moderation of Reclaimed Slur Usage
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.10327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As Perspective API is deprecated, platforms are turning to large language models for content moderation, encoding policy as natural language that the model must interpret at inference time. Reclaimed slurs test this design directly. The same term can express in-group pride or target the community that reclaimed it, and misreading it silences the speech moderation is meant to protect. We audit four general-purpose LLMs and four moderation-specific systems, with Perspective API as a legacy baseline, on IYKYK, a corpus of reclaimed and derogatory usage of three slurs annotated by community members. Across the policy, decision, reasoning, disparity, and steering layers of this audit, we find that whether a system was purpose-built for moderation explains little about how it handles reclaimed language. No system reliably agrees with community judgment, and all fail most on language reclaimed within Black communities. What separates systems is instead how their policy is represented. Only systems whose policy is expressed in the prompt can be steered at all, and even then, explicit definitions change how models justify a decision more than how they make it. We argue that policy transparency determines whether moderation failures can be corrected, but that correcting them requires contextual judgment that definitions supplied at inference time cannot provide.

ai.title: Distinguishing Extraction Failures and Clinical Discordance with LLM Uncertainty on Radiology Reports
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.10502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can structure clinical datasets, but extraction error must be distinguished from discordance in the underlying data. From a real-world cohort of 1{,}045 patients undergoing coronary CT angiography (CCTA), we evaluated whether LLM uncertainty during vessel-level coronary artery disease (CAD) stenosis extraction could identify extraction failure and clinical discordance. References were expert CCTA annotations (253 patients) and subsequent invasive coronary angiography (ICA; 729 patients). We quantify extraction failure as disagreement between stenosis severity in LLM extracted versus expert annotations, and clinical discordance as disagreement in stenosis severity between CCTA and subsequent ICA. Stenosis Margin, selected from ten candidate measures, was used to quantify LLM uncertainty, and generalized estimating equation logistic regression and AUC evaluated its association and incremental discrimination for each failure mode. LLM uncertainty was strongly associated with extraction failure (adjusted OR 4.15 [95% CI 2.57--6.69], $P<0.001$) and substantially improved discrimination beyond LLM-extracted CCTA stenosis severity alone (AUC 0.81 to 0.86; $\Delta$AUC $+0.06$ [$+0.03$, $+0.09$], $P=0.001$). For example, for a covered nasal spray that costs $150, enrollees would pay about $38 or $53, depending on whether their coinsurance rate was 25 percent or 35 percent. ai.title: Democracy Assistance: State Department Should Improve Congressional Notification of Its Use of Certain Legal Authorities
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Federal law contains certain provisions, known as notwithstanding authorities, that allow agencies to provide funding that would otherwise be restricted. Historically, the annual appropriations act has required agencies to notify Congress if they intend to use a notwithstanding authority to provide assistance in countries where U.S. law prohibits U.S. funding. In fiscal years (FY) 2023 and 2024, the joint explanatory statement (JES) accompanying the act included additional directions for providing such notifications. In July 2025 the Secretary of State announced that USAID had ceased to implement foreign assistance. State assumed certain former USAID functions, including some democracy programs, and will submit congressional notifications related to future democracy assistance. While Congress has not included a JES with directions for providing information on notwithstanding authorities with every appropriations act, it did so in fiscal year 2026 and may continue to do so in the future. GAO’s review of 37 State congressional notifications for FYs 2023 and 2024 funding found that 36 of the notifications do not address one of three criteria, specified in Section 7015(c) of the FYs 2023 and 2024 appropriations acts or in their JESs, for reporting the use of notwithstanding authorities. ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Department of Homeland Security (DHS) detention facility inspections have changed at the same time that the number of immigration detention facilities and the size of the detained population have increased. From April 2025 to April 2026, following a January 2025 Executive Order, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) added over 40 detention facilities that detain noncitizens for over 72 hours. The average daily population of detained noncitizens grew by over 50 percent, to 61,817 individuals, over the timeframe. From fiscal year 2024 to July 2026, three of the four DHS entities that conducted inspections changed the frequency (decreased or increased) or stopped conducting inspections. Changes to Inspections Conducted by DHS Entities from Fiscal Year (FY) 2024 to July 2026 ICE relies on these inspections to identify deficiencies in its facilities and ensure compliance with its detention standards. However, the frequency of inspections has in some cases decreased, there is an increased reliance on self-inspections, and processes for these inspections have changed. ICE has not used evidence, such as data on deficiencies identified through inspections and performance information such as the extent to which facilities are in compliance with their contracts, to determine the effects of these recent changes on facility conditions. ai.source_name: 歐盟執委會 數位政策
ai.via: 歐盟執委會 數位政策
ai.raw_summary: Commission preliminarily finds TikTok’s ‘For You’ feed in breach of Digital Services Act for harmful ‘rabbit holes’ effect Anonymous (not verified) Fri, 11/06/2026 - 12:09 The European Commission has preliminarily found TikTok in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) for the so-called ‘rabbit hole effect’ of its recommender system. TikTok's ‘For You' feed shows users a continuous stream of personalised videos, even when those are related to mental health struggles and body image. The more a user interacts with a certain type of content, the more TikTok's ‘For You' feed algorithm recommends similar content. This design can be harmful when such endless and repeated exposure involves, for example, content about sadness, isolation or body image. These ‘rabbit holes' can have a detrimental impact on users' mental health, especially that of vulnerable adults and minors. These preliminary findings focus on both risk assessment and mitigation measures. Read the full details in the press release Find further information about: Supervision of the designated very large online platforms and search engines under DSA Digital Services Act - main aspects of the regulation User rights under the Digital Services Act - an overview Related topics Online platforms and e-commerce DSA - Digital Services Act

The feedback is being gathered through a call for evidence . The responses collected through the call for evidence will help shape guidelines aimed at ensuring that advertising repositories meet the needs of their users. Amongst other things, the guidelines will advise on: how to make advertising repositories easily searchable how to provide insights on how users are targeted and reached how to make the content of advertisements accessible Once adopted, these guidelines will aim to ensure that the advertising repositories provided by very large online platforms (VLOPs) and very large online search engines (VLOSEs) are effective and fit for purpose. Effective advertising repositories are essential tools for enabling greater public scrutiny of online advertising. Transparency in advertising – revealing who pays and how citizens are targeted – helps to protect public health, ensure a high level of consumer protection and safeguard the integrity of elections. Advertising repositories also support effective supervision and enforcement of the DSA. Next steps The call for evidence will be followed by a targeted public consultation in 2027. trade.raw_summary: 經濟部今（9）日召開貿易救濟審議會，會中就我國對韓國及中國大陸冷軋扁軋非方向性電磁鋼品反傾銷案，以及對中國大陸特定鋁箔課徵反傾銷稅屆滿5年之落日調查案等2案之產業損害調查結果進行審議，前者最後認定國內產業遭受實質損害；後者認定國內產業損害可能因停止課徵反傾銷稅而繼續或再發生。 經濟部表示，就電磁鋼品案調查發現，韓國及中國大陸涉案貨物進口量大幅增加且持續降價，自112年起以低於國產品價格銷售，國內產業為維持競爭力被迫跟進減價，惟因減價幅度不及涉案傾銷貨物而流失客戶，導致生產量、產能利用率、內銷量、市場占有率等經濟指標全面下滑，並自113年起內銷出現虧損且逐步擴大。雖然國內產業114年相關經濟指標一度改善，但115年上半年再度轉弱，顯示涉案傾銷貨物進口已對國內產業造成顯著不利影響。 另針對中國大陸特定鋁箔落日調查案，調查發現，課徵反傾銷稅期間涉案貨物進口量雖有減少，但仍以低價與國產品競爭，使得國內產業營運狀況略有好轉後又再度惡化。復考量中國大陸鋁箔產能過剩且出口能力強勁，加上越來越多國家對其鋁箔採行貿易救濟措施或提高關稅，已嚴重限縮其外銷市場。若我國停止課徵反傾銷稅，涉案貨物可能再度低價大量出口至鄰近且其已建立行銷通路的我國市場。在國內需求尚未好轉、產業體質仍然脆弱的情況下，可能使我國特定鋁箔產業之損害繼續或再發生。 經濟部表示，上述2案產業損害認定結果將通知財政部，並由該部提交關稅稅率審議小組審議是否課徵及繼續課徵反傾銷稅。該2案之產業損害調查報告公開版可於今年12月9日起至貿易署網站（網址：https://www.trade.gov.tw/）「經貿往來」/「我國採行之貿易救濟措施」/「案件調查」項下之「調查報告」下載。 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：綜合企劃組邱組長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7361

trade.title: 進口人無償或減價提供賣方用於生產及銷售進口貨物之物品或勞務，應計入完稅價格申報
trade.source_name: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.via: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 海關近來接獲進口人詢問國外自備模具之費用是否應計入完稅價格等問題，關務署表示，倘進口人有「無償」或「減價」提供賣方用於生產或銷售該進口貨物之物品或勞務，應主動將其計入完稅價格向海關申報，避免因未申報相關費用而須補稅或送查價，影響通關速度。 關務署說明，依據關稅法第29條規定，進口貨物之完稅價格以交易價格為課徵關稅基礎，為確保完稅價格核估之正確性，若進口貨物之實付或應付價格中，未計入下列由買方無償或減價提供賣方用於生產或銷售該貨物之物品及勞務，應將其合理攤計之金額或減價金額計入完稅價格： 一、組成該進口貨物之原材料、零組件及其類似品。 二、生產該進口貨物所需之工具、鑄模、模型及其類似品。 三、生產該進口貨物所消耗之材料。 四、生產該進口貨物在國外之工程、開發、工藝、設計及其類似勞務。 關務署提醒，倘進口人有此類產銷協助費用，應提供買賣合約書、商業發票、付款證明等必要文件供海關審核，若無客觀及可計量之資料，海關將依關稅法第29條第4項規定無法按交易價格核估其完稅價格，籲請進口人注意，避免海關查核時發現短（漏）報，影響自身權益。 新聞稿聯絡人：賴科長 聯絡電話：（02）25505500分機2703

trade.title: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office: Patent Backlog Reduction Efforts Pose Risks to Examiner Retention and Examination Quality
trade.raw_summary: What GAO Found The backlog of unexamined patent applications awaiting an initial decision from the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) rose to about 838,000 applications in January 2025. In September 2025, the USPTO announced a goal to reduce the backlog to under 599,000 applications but did not specify a time frame for reaching it. The backlog was last at that level in 2020. To reduce the backlog, the USPTO is requiring patent examiners to review more applications, has decreased examiner training, and has expanded the use of AI patent search tools. As of August 2026, the USPTO reduced the backlog to about 756,000 applications, but average applicant wait times for a final patentability decision had increased by 11 percent since January 2025. GAO’s analysis found that, even with examiners doing more work, the USPTO is unlikely to reduce the backlog to under 599,000 patent applications before 2031 without lowering examiner attrition (see figure). The examiner attrition rate increased from 2.9 percent in fiscal year 2020 to 7.6 percent in fiscal year 2025. The agency is seeking to hire more examiners, but if high examiner attrition continues, it will affect the USPTO’s ability to reduce the backlog. As of August 2026, the 12-month examiner attrition rate was 7.6 percent.
